narrative: Material PL1__MBDEC0A8 exhibits highly intermittent and lumpy demand (CV=1.14) with 38% zero-demand working days, indicating a compound-Poisson-like process with irregular large orders. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.27) with observed spikes to 13.6 days, generating substantial lead-time demand variance. The (r,Q) policy is recommended: a reorder point of 9,949 units and order quantity of 9,905 units (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 12,689). The current SAP safety stock of 297 units is critically insufficient and must be raised to 4,380 units to achieve the 95% service level target.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ of 12689 reduced to 9905 to satisfy safety_stock + order_quantity <= max_storage_units (14285.93).
Increasing order frequency slightly above pure EOQ optimum; capacity review recommended.
3 demand observations winsorised at upper bound 3340.18 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given intermittent/lumpy demand and unstable lead times, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy provides responsive replenishment triggered by inventory position crossing the reorder point, avoiding the inefficiency of fixed-interval reviews when demand timing is unpredictable. EOQ minimises total order+holding cost given annual demand of 209,266 units.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 14,286 units binds at current safety stock level (4,380 + 9,905 = 14,285 <= 14,286). Any increase in safety stock would require a corresponding reduction in order quantity below MOQ or a facility capacity upgrade. Service level may be marginally degraded if a larger order is blocked.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None under current parameters. If safety stock requirements increase (e.g. higher service level or more variable lead times), MOQ + safety_stock may approach or exceed max_storage_units, requiring escalation to facilities and procurement.
